claims.text: Equimolar CoCrFeNiTi can exist as a single-phase FCC alloy.
The proposed starting CoCrFeNiTi alloy is fully random and has no significant short-range order.
Equimolar CoCrFeNiTi has relatively low hardness and strength while retaining favorable plasticity and machinability.
The absence of short-range order is the cause of the relatively low hardness and strength of equimolar CoCrFeNiTi.
A random atomic distribution in equimolar CoCrFeNiTi produces a relatively uniform and lower Peierls barrier.
Localized regions of high Peierls friction can repeatedly pin gliding dislocations and produce wavy dislocation lines and jagged motion.
The density of regions with high local Peierls friction is proportional to the critical stress for dislocation glide and affects dislocation mobility.
A lower Peierls barrier permits easier dislocation glide in the base CoCrFeNiTi alloy.
Easier dislocation glide causes favorable plasticity and machinability but lower hardness and strength.
A modest increase in Ti content promotes incipient short-range order in CoCrFeNiTi.
A suitable thermal treatment can induce short-range order in CoCrFeNiTi.
Short-range order creates localized lattice distortions that increase local Peierls friction.
Short-range-order-induced regions of elevated Peierls friction act as obstacles to dislocation motion.
CoCrFeNiTi alloys with increased Ti content can remain single-phase FCC.
Increasing Ti above the equimolar CoCrFeNiTi composition will increase hardness relative to the equimolar alloy.
Increasing Ti or inducing short-range order will increase compressive strength relative to the equimolar alloy.
The modified alloy will exhibit more pronounced dislocation pinning and more wavy or jagged dislocation lines than the starting alloy.
Strengthening through short-range order may reduce ductility.
The proposed mechanism remains operative under compressive loading from 25 °C to as high as 600 °C.
Phase separation or dominant precipitation hardening would place the alloy outside the proposed short-range-order mechanism.

contradictions.description: Reduced ductility is presented only as a possible outcome, and its magnitude is explicitly said to remain uncertain, yet unchanged plasticity is declared sufficient to falsify the hypothesis.
